<!-- pr-reviewer: 864a0fb8bdf309b4091dc8be52fe523a1affe6c9 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge** (one test goes red once the PR is merged with current main; the design itself checks out).

Thanks for the careful decision file. Reviewed at 864a0fb8, trial-merged with upstream/main 1c539b6b (clean merge, no conflicts).

**What looks good**
- `docs/decisions/388-per-setup-mount.md` inventories the readers. I grepped the remaining `machine::of` / `kind_of` / `post_of` callers (not `of_setup`); all that are left on the active mount are ribbon, Setup/Machine/Post pages, machine editor, debug info, `set_machine_mode`, `spindle_row`, `post_options`, or `posting_mounts::active` (empty-program fallback), and the ones the doc names carry reasons.
- No build.rs, `.github/`, scripts or dependency changes; only `cam.d.ts` is an asset-side change. New module has a provenance line and is 252 lines. No new `unwrap`/`expect` in `posting_mounts.rs`.
- Single-mount output unchanged: `posting` (17), `fixtures` (14), `axis_direction` (12), `setup_mount` (6), `setup_carry` (9), `rest_across_setups` (7) all pass on the merged tree, and the one-mount post paths go through the same joins.
- Keeping the stricter #404 carry refusal (`one_machine`, mill-to-different-mill refused) is right: material must not cross a machine change, and a refusal is the safe direction. It is recorded in the decision file and the PR comment.

**Local results (merged with main)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| build `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` | ok |
| setup_mounts_post | 4 pass, 1 FAIL |
| setup_mount / setup_carry / rest_across_setups / posting / fixtures / axis_direction / mcp / mcp_setup | all pass |
| ui `--lib` | 344 pass, 1 fail: `headless_run_succeeds` (no GPU adapter on this machine; environment artifact, not the PR) |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

UI snapshot suites were not run.

```
thread 'a_travel_limit_is_judged_on_the_ops_own_machine_only' panicked at crates/app/tests/setup_mounts_post.rs:260:9:
assertion `left == right` failed: one machine is outrun (Setup2 active): []
  left: 0
 right: 1
```
At the PR head alone (without main) all 5 pass, so this is a main-vs-test interaction, not a code bug.

**Requested before merge**
1. `crates/app/tests/setup_mounts_post.rs:237-262`: the test assumes the shipped "VMC 3-axis" Z stroke ends at 0 so the face at z=19.5 outruns it. Main's #477 (VMC Z stroke in program coordinates, 12848ffc / 37524a26) changed that stroke, so no limit problem is reported any more. Please merge `origin/main`, then move the test's face depth (or give Setup1 an explicit short-stroke machine as `bench_mill()` does) so one machine is genuinely outrun, and re-run.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- `crates/app/src/mcp/fixture_tools.rs:97`: `get_fixture_findings` reports `"machine"` from `machine::of(w)` (active) while `workholding_view` is per setup. Worth a line in the decision file (or per-setup machines in that field).
- `posting.rs` is 1111 lines; this PR shrinks it slightly, so fine.
- The tool-number clash over-refusal across machines is already tracked in #438.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 1840a687febfcf5bdc4317effb86d32da2b83aef -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- `posting_mounts.rs` (252 lines, provenance line present, no unwrap/expect/panic): a one-mount program takes the old single-file path unchanged; several mounts are all judged (scripts read, program gate, per-mount work-offset register check) before `write_all` writes anything, so a refusal writes nothing.
- WCS stays single-sourced: `posting_wcs_slot::wcs_slot` only delegates to `crate::setup::wcs_slot`; no second derivation added. One WCS per setup is still enforced per mount via `shared_word_problems_in`.
- Each mount's file carries only the ops whose effective setup belongs to that mount, in program order (`program_mounts` walks `operation_order`, skips suppressed ops, groups by machine+post), run through that mount's own script and machine.
- Machine limit/inverted-axis checks run per mount on that mount's ops (`machine_checks`), so an op is never judged on another setup's machine. The retired "activate SetupN first" refusal is replaced by tests of the new behaviour.
- No project-format change in the diff, so no migration or breaking marker is needed. No build.rs, .github, scripts, dependency, snapshot PNG, golden or CHANGELOG edits.

**Local results (merged with current main; clean auto-merge)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| setup_mounts_post | 5 passed |
| setup_mount | 6 passed |
| fixtures | 14 passed |
| axis_direction | 12 passed |
| posting | 17 passed |
| setups / setup_wcs / setup_relative / setup_carry | 11 / 7 / 9 / 9 passed |
| golden_cl | 23 passed |
| post_not_judged | 4 passed |
| clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings | clean |

Not run: ui suites (display-only UI changes), snapshots (ignored lane).

**Requested before merge:** none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- `post_each` (posting_mounts.rs) filters each mount's streams by op name; it does not assert that the per-mount op counts sum to the program's op count. A cheap internal check would turn any future grouping drift into a named refusal rather than a silently missing op.
- Same-machine setups separated by another machine's setup (mill, lathe, mill) land in one mount's file in program order; worth a test if not already covered.
- Tool-number clash (#221) is still judged program-wide across machines (tracked as #438); no real-machine run of the multi-file output, as the PR states.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
